rows.grounds: binding device; first term of emphatic fourfold repetition
ensnaring mesh; second emphatic repetition of the same term
capturing device; third emphatic repetition of the same term
identifies the snare with the deer-eyed one from prior context

items.question: What binding force is emphatically identified as the captor of the lord-deer?
premises: The lord-deer has come into bondage.
The same term for snare is repeated four times.
The final repetition identifies the snare with the female subject.
items.inference: The deer-eyed woman herself is the inescapable snare that binds.
uncertainties: Whether the fourth vāgurā functions as predicate identifying her or as a vocative-like exclamation is contextually inferred.
items.plain_english: Snare, net, trap—she is the snare.
